approved: Export Control Amendment (Banning Cotton Exports to Ensure Water Security) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would prohibit exporting cotton grown in Australia to protect water and food supplies in the Murray-Darling Basin.
It would add a provision to the Export Control Act 1982 that, three years after it starts, regulations must treat Australian cotton as a banned export good.
The ban would not affect cotton produced for use within Australia.
The bill bans all exports of Australian-grown cotton.
The ban takes effect three years after the provision commences.
Cotton grown for domestic use is not affected.
Cotton growers, exporters and governments of the Murray-Darling Basin states and territory.
